publisher: International AI Safety Report (DSIT / AI Security Institute, chaired by Yoshua Bengio)
title: International AI Safety Report 2026 - Executive Summary (DSIT 2026/001)
key_claim: Early evidence suggests that reliance on AI tools can weaken critical thinking skills and encourage 'automation bias', the tendency to trust AI system outputs without sufficient scrutiny; current AI systems also exhibit reliability failures and AI agents act autonomously, making human intervention harder; early labour evidence shows declining demand for early-career workers in some AI-exposed occupations such as writing.
verbatim_quote: reliance on AI tools can weaken critical thinking skills and encourage 'automation bias'
notes: Tier 1 multilateral / government-commissioned report (30+ countries, EU/OECD/UN nominees, 100+ experts). Structural anchor (3-6m band). Anchors the human-autonomy / skill-erosion risk and the early-career-demand signal.

title: AI and the euro area economy - keynote speech by Philip R. Lane
key_claim: Micro-level deployment evidence is encouraging: access to ChatGPT reduced time on mid-level professional writing tasks by 40 percent and raised output quality by 18 percent, with the largest gains accruing to lower-ability workers, and a generative AI assistant raised customer-support issues resolved per hour by 15 percent; but aggregate productivity follows a delayed J-curve.
notes: Tier 1 central-bank primary source. Used for the consensus framing (AI productivity gains are real, concentrated in lower-ability workers) and the productivity-lag J-curve.

title: The 2026 AI Index Report - Economy chapter
date_evidence: The Stanford AI Index 2026 was published April 13, 2026, by Stanford's Human-Centered AI Institute (HAI).
key_claim: AI productivity gains are largest in structured, measurable work (14-15% in customer support, 26% in software development, 73% in marketing output), but recent evidence raises concerns that heavy AI reliance may carry long-term learning penalties that slow skill development over time; employment for software developers aged 22-25 has fallen nearly 20% from 2024.
verbatim_quote: heavy AI reliance may carry long-term learning penalties that slow skill development over time
notes: Tier 2 academic data compilation. Pairs the real productivity gains (the consensus) with the learning-penalty caveat (the signal) and the junior-developer employment fall.

title: AI Assistance Reduces Persistence and Hurts Independent Performance
key_claim: Across randomized controlled trials on human-AI interactions (N=1,222), AI assistance improves performance in the short term but people perform significantly worse without AI and are more likely to give up; effects emerge after only brief interactions (~10-15 minutes); persistence costs are concentrated among those who obtain direct solutions; the authors call this the first large-scale causal evidence of AI-induced deskilling, noting persistence is foundational to skill acquisition.
verbatim_quote: people perform significantly worse without AI and are more likely to give up
notes: Tier 2 academic preprint (UCLA). Causal core of the signal: AI dependence erodes unassisted performance and persistence; the answer-vs-hint distinction informs the counter-counter.

title: How AI is changing the nature of entry level work
date_evidence: How AI is changing the nature of entry level work Mar 26, 2026
key_claim: US entry-level job postings have fallen by about 35% in 18 months, in large part because of AI (Revelio Labs); cutting junior talent yields short-term efficiency but masks longer-term risks - slower AI adoption, weakened succession plans and stalled knowledge transfer; entry-level work is being reshaped from task execution toward reviewing and monitoring AI outputs.
notes: Tier 2 institutional (WEF; bylined by Cognizant's Chief People Officer). Supplies the organisational mechanism: the entry-level apprenticeship rung where foundational skill is built is being automated and re-pointed at AI-output review.

title: 2026 Work Trend Index Annual Report - Agents, human agency and the opportunity for every organization
date_evidence: meta-article:modified_time: 2026-05-13T18:40:06+00:00 ... Microsoft 2026 Work Trend Index Annual Report
key_claim: Microsoft frames a 'Transformation Paradox' - workers are ready for AI but organisations are not - and argues AI 'expands who can do high-value work', shifting from expertise to agency; it reports that the biggest factor behind AI impact is organisational (culture, management, talent practices) rather than individual capability, and that most users treat AI output as a starting point rather than a final answer.
notes: Tier 4 vendor survey (20,000 workers, 10 countries), used as directional corroboration and as the optimistic counter-case (AI as capability-democratiser, not deskiller).

title: Is AI Making Our Brains Weaker?
date_evidence: Is AI Making Our Brains Weaker? — TIME, May 19, 2026 (time.com/article/2026/05/19/is-ai-making-our-brains-weaker)
key_claim: Quality-journalism synthesis of the growing body of experimental evidence that heavy AI reliance is associated with weaker independent reasoning and cognitive offloading, signalling that the deskilling concern has moved from academic circles into mainstream executive attention.
notes: Tier 3 quality journalism. Used for public-salience corroboration that the deskilling evidence is reaching boards and policymakers.
